sentences.text: Rupephaps was a member of the bird family Columbidae, commonly known as pigeons.
Its genus name combines the Polynesian word 'Rupe' and the Greek word 'phaps', both meaning pigeon.
This species was the first pigeon described from pre-Pliocene fossil deposits in the Australasian region.
Known as the Saint Bathans pigeon, it is an extinct species from the Miocene of New Zealand.
The species was described from a left coracoid fossil collected in 2008 near the Manuherikia River in Central Otago.
Rupephaps lived during the Late Early Miocene epoch.
It existed between 18.7 and 15.9 million years ago, spanning the Burdigalian to Langhian stages.
